stemMd: A satellite moves in a circular orbit at constant speed. Which statement about its acceleration is correct?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It points away from the centre.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It is directed toward the centre of the orbit.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It is zero because speed is constant.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It points in one fixed direction throughout the orbit.

options.label: E
options.textMd: It points along the motion at every instant.

explanationMd: Acceleration measures change in velocity, which includes direction as well as speed. Circular motion requires inward centripetal acceleration. Constant speed removes tangential acceleration but does not remove the acceleration needed to bend the path.

distractorRationale.c: Velocity changes direction even when its magnitude is constant.
distractorRationale.e: Tangential acceleration would change the speed.
distractorRationale.a: That would not produce the inward curvature of the orbit.
distractorRationale.d: The inward direction changes as the satellite moves.
